2.  This anticipatory bail application under Sections 482 and 484 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, has been preferred by the petitioner apprehending his arrest for offences registered under Sections 376 and 493 of the Indian Penal Code.
3. The allegation against this petitioner is that on the pretext of marriage he has entered into physical relationship with the informant.
4. Today at the time of hearing, learned counsel for the victim has appeared and stated that the parties are residing together as husband and wife as they have contracted their marriage.
5. Considering the fact that the parties are now married and staying together, this Court finds it a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.
6. Accordingly, this Anticipatory Bail Application stands allowed.

The petitioner, above named, is directed to surrender before the learned court below within four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order and on the event of his surrender or arrest, he shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount Xxx vs The State Of Jharkhand on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101329781/
1 each, to the satisfaction of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Palamau at Daltonganj, in connection 2025:JHHC:18409 with Daltonganj Town P.S. Case No.25 of 2021, subject to the condition that one of the bailers should be a close relative of the petitioner and other should be a resident of State of Jharkhand, having sufficient landed property in his/her name or in the name of his/her ancestors in which he/she is having share and to that effect, he/she has to file an affidavit before the Trial Court indicating his/her share in the property.
